A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PaperCoder research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison; relocated and renumbered material can be matched.

before.justification: v4 reports original benchmark evaluations, author assessments, ablations and execution/reproduction studies in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v5 retains those original results and adds environment-setup, repair-effort and cross-family evaluator analyses in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The planning–analysis–coding pipeline, Self-Refine variant and debugging procedure are retained. Appendix B.6 adds an experimental environment-setup prompting extension that generates installation and execution commands (Figure 33). Generating reproduce.sh for PaperBench was already described in v4; a dedicated DevOps agent remains future work.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Paper2CodeBench, PaperBench/Code-Dev, human-evaluation papers and reproduction cases. The additional checks reuse subsets of these collections, retaining the same ML paper-implementation coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain Abstract, Paper, ChatDev and MetaGPT on Paper2CodeBench, and BasicAgent and IterativeAgent on PaperBench. Gemini-Flash2.5 is introduced as an evaluator, not as a competing code-generation method.

E3.justification: Existing main evaluation settings are retained. Supplementary protocols add environment-setup testing on 30 papers, Gemini cross-family judging on 30 randomly selected papers, difficulty-weighted edit counts, and GPT-5.1 categorization of repair traces (Appendices B.2, B.6 and B.9).

E4.justification: v5 substantially expands diagnostic analysis with an environment-dependency intervention, cross-family evaluator validation, developer-effort estimates and iteration-level repair traces. Figure 7 adds a concrete architecture-versus-logic-design case study. Existing ablations, refinement experiments, methodology-removal tests and reproduction analyses remain present.

E5.justification: Evaluation sampling and averaging, standard-deviation reporting, three-run PaperBench reporting with its o1/o3 exceptions, and significance reporting are unchanged. Added repair-iteration counts and correlation point estimates introduce no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark, ablation and reproduction results retain their values. New findings include Gemini/o3-mini Spearman correlation of 0.73, no dependency-related failures in the 30-paper setup experiment, developer-effort proxy scores of 5/6/27/53/22, and repair traces spanning 2–11 iterations (Tables 11 and 14). Table 17 adds author quotations.

T1.justification: Appendix B.2 introduces a numerical definition for estimated developer effort: modified-line counts weighted by a difficulty factor of 1–3. This limited metric definition supplements unchanged task and pipeline mathematics in Section 3; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same three-stage contribution, comparative superiority, author-usefulness findings and reproduction-assistance claims. Changes from 'functional' to 'operational' and from 'strong' to 'practical' executability do not materially change their scientific scope.

C2.justification: New appendix discussions address contamination risk, evaluator-family bias, repair effort and the priority given to methodological fidelity over environment automation. Appendix C makes the existing visual-input future direction more concrete through OCR suggestions. The principal interpretations and existing domain limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Figure 33 supplies the environment-script prompt, while Figures 8–12 disclose additional model identifiers, configuration changes, data paths and API fixes for existing reproduction cases. Core implementation and hardware details in Appendix A remain unchanged; the expanded patches do not establish that earlier experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: v5 adds document-parsing/OCR references, including MinerU, MonkeyOCR and DeepSeek-OCR, to the visual-input discussion, plus references for previously included case-study papers. Section 2's related-work narrative and research positioning remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most main prose and all existing prompt texts are retained. Changes include localized wording edits, additional appendix subsections, updated cross-references, author-affiliation/advising information and acknowledgements, without extensive rewriting of the existing narrative.

P2.justification: The appendix gains substantial visual documentation: developer-effort, repair-trace and author-response tables, an ablation illustration and an environment-prompt figure. The two earlier debugging illustrations become five expanded diff-style figures. Existing main tables and plots are retained but regrouped and repositioned.

improvement.justification: The added cross-family evaluation, environment test and explicit repair documentation modestly strengthen validation and transparency beyond v4. The gains are limited: 'developer time' is an uncalibrated edit-count proxy, and Table 14 includes memory optimization and algorithmic refactoring despite prose emphasizing simple fixes. The core empirical evidence remains unchanged.
